To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a PET bottle-to-bottle-recycling process can be designed to meet the requirements of the European food law.

the investigated PET recycling process is able to produce PET recyclates with concentrations of contaminants below the threshold levels of the EU food law and therefore is able to comply with the requirements of EU food law.
a PET-recycling plant with the process option of producing PET preforms is not suitable for recycling PET bottles for food-contact applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) the evaluation of the cleaning efficiency of the investigated PET recycling process, (b) the evaluation of a challenge test for an inline recycling process, and (c) the compliance of the PET-recyclate with food law.
the development and implementation of a challenge test for a PET-recycling plant with the aim of demonstrating compliance with food law.
the evaluation of the efficiency of an inline PET-recycling process with regard to the removal of contaminants and the compliance of the recyclate with food safety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the investigated PET-recycle process is not suitable for the production of PET bottles intended for the direct contact with food.
the PET-recycling process investigated in this study is not suitable for the production of food-contact PET containers.
the investigated PET-recycled material can be considered safe for direct food contact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the investigated recycling process for PET bottles is suitable to produce PET recyclate for direct food contact.
the investigated recycling process is suitable for the production of PET preform and bottle material for direct food contact application.

a PET-recycling plant with a predecontaminating-extruder combination and a pelletizing system at the end of the process can be considered as a safe process for the production of food-contact PET recyclate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inline process is not a critical process in terms to food safety and the consumer protection.
a challenge test of the PET recycling process should be carried out with the final product of the recycling process and should be designed to reflect the specific conditions of the process.
, for the evaluation of the inline recycling process, a challenge test has to be developed, which is able to simulate a worst case situation.
